builder_plan.scenario: A multi-step product task fails because the agent loses track of dependencies.
builder_plan.change: Try the proposed planning step on tasks with checkable intermediate outcomes.
builder_plan.baseline: The same agent solving the same tasks without the new planning step.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task completion, unnecessary steps, planning tokens, response time, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Beyond Weight Updates: Evolving Agent Harnesses for Domain Specialization
summary: It replaces RL/SFT weight updates for domain specialization with evolutionary optimization of the agent harness (system prompt, tool schemas, skill library, planning scaffolding) around a frozen policy, using GEPA as the outer-loop optimizer. Cost is inference-time reflection and evaluation rollouts for the evolutionary loop, no GPU training; harnesses are loadable per domain and compose with later weight-based RL. Risks: gains depend on having a reliable task evaluator and sufficient trajectory budget, evolved harnesses may overfit to the benchmark-like evaluation distribution, and the paper itself finds weight updates still give the strongest single-path gains, so harness-only specialization has a ceiling.
rationale: The method requires no GPU training, works with frozen API-served models, and is evaluated on agentic coding and tool-use benchmarks, making it directly adoptable under the reader's constraints as a first specialization step before any fine-tuning.
technique: Evolutionary optimization of agent harnesses (prompts, tools, scaffolding)

claims.statement: It replaces RL/SFT weight updates for domain specialization with evolutionary optimization of the agent harness (system prompt, tool schemas, skill library, planning scaffolding) around a frozen policy, using GEPA as the outer-loop optimizer. Cost is inference-time reflection and evaluation rollouts for the evolutionary loop, no GPU training; harnesses are loadable per domain and compose with later weight-based RL. Risks: gains depend on having a reliable task evaluator and sufficient trajectory budget, evolved harnesses may overfit to the benchmark-like evaluation distribution, and the paper itself finds weight updates still give the strongest single-path gains, so harness-only specialization has a ceiling.

The paper reports that harness evolution recovers most of the gains of weight-based RL/SFT on SWE-bench Verified, OfficeBench, and Terminal-Bench at a small fraction of the compute, and that combining harness evolution with weight updates is best overall; no numeric factor is stated in the abstract.
